title: A non-Gaussian massive continuum theory from the planar O(3) model
exact_target: For the nearest-neighbor square-lattice O(3) spin model, can one choose dyadic $L>1$, $H>0$, $a_N=L^{-N}$, $\beta _N=H+(\log $ L)/(2pi)N+O(log(N+1)) and field factors $B_N$ so that all smeared field laws and Schwinger moments converge to an O(3)-invariant, Euclidean-invariant, reflection-positive clustering theory? Require factorial distribution bounds, reconstruction of a local unitary 1+1-dimensional theory with unique vacuum and positive spectral gap, and a nonzero connected four-point function on separated time supports.
